title: F5 BIG-IP: five critical TMM flaws in iRules and APM (Nov 2026)
summary: F5 published fixes on 18 November 2026 for five critical BIG-IP data-plane vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-121805, CVE-2026-120292, CVE-2026-120285, CVE-2026-116953, CVE-2026-123637) plus a high-severity APM SAML denial of service (CVE-2026-126822). Each critical issue is only reachable in a specific configuration: iRules that use PEM::subscriber, MR::message route, PSC::ip_address or GENERICMESSAGE::route, or an APM per-request policy with the Client Information and Endpoint Security agents. In those configurations an unauthenticated remote request can crash the Traffic Management Microkernel and may lead to code execution; F5 says there is no control-plane exposure and lists no mitigations beyond the fixes. They are not in KEV and F5 has not reported exploitation.

cves.note: Condition: iRule using PEM::subscriber on a virtual server. CVSS 4.0 9.3 (F5). F5 K000163946.
Condition: HTTP profile plus iRule using MR::message route. CVSS 4.0 9.3 (F5). F5 K000163940.
Condition: HTTP profile plus iRule using PSC::ip_address. CVSS 4.0 9.3 (F5). F5 K000163939.
Condition: iRule using GENERICMESSAGE::route. CVSS 4.0 9.3 (F5). F5 K000163941.
Condition: APM per-request policy with Client Information and Endpoint Security agents. CVSS 4.0 9.3 (F5). F5 K000163937.
APM access profile configured as SAML SP: TMM restart (DoS only). CVSS 4.0 8.7 (F5). F5 K000163942.

impact: Unauthenticated denial of service of the data plane (TMM restart) and possible remote code execution on BIG-IP in the affected configurations.
action: Check whether your virtual servers use the listed iRule commands or APM agents; if so, install the F5 fixes from the K articles now.
affected: BIG-IP with the iRule commands or APM configurations named in each CVE; affected and fixed versions per the F5 K article for each CVE (not copied here)
fixed: Fixed releases and engineering hotfixes listed in F5 K000163937, K000163939, K000163940, K000163941, K000163942 and K000163946
steps: Export the iRules on every BIG-IP and search for PEM::subscriber, MR::message route, PSC::ip_address and GENERICMESSAGE::route.
List APM per-request policies that include Client Information and Endpoint Security agents, and access profiles acting as SAML SP.
Patch the exposed systems first, using the version matrix in each K article.
Watch CISA KEV and F5 for exploitation; F5 bugs have been exploited quickly before (for example CVE-2026-94127 in September).
pitfalls: Assuming the management interface lockdown helps: these are data-plane issues on the virtual servers.
Patching only APM: four of the five critical bugs are in iRules on any module that runs them.

sources.title: BleepingComputer: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
